$comment: THE DECLARED GOVERNANCE MODE. This file is the single source; CLAUDE.md describes it
in prose and CODEOWNERS routes reviews under it, but neither of those is authoritative.
It exists because 'we are in development mode' was true, load-bearing, and written
down nowhere. CODEOWNERS asserted that review was enforced - citing NIST SP 800-171
3.4.3 and 3.1.5 - while the ruleset required zero approvals, so a reader or a
cold-starting agent believed in a control that did not exist. A mode nobody can read
is not a policy, and a policy nothing checks is a wish.
verification/layer-01-audit.ps1 V1.5 reads this file and the LIVE branch ruleset and
fails when they disagree, so declaring operational mode without flipping the setting
rationale: The solution is still being built. Intent for a change is established by the person
building it, and the gauntlet - lint, both test suites, CodeQL, gitleaks, Trivy - is
the safety gate. Agents are authorized to self-approve and merge their own pull
Nothing here reaches a production system or a real user. The estate is synthetic,
disposable by design, and rebuilt on demand.

when: the estate serves a real user, a real workload, or a real auditor's evidence, OR
anyone outside the build team depends on its output
transition.action: Set required_approving_review_count to 1 on the branch ruleset for main. V1.5 fails until this matches the declared mode.
consequence: Agents lose self-approval. A human approves changes to the paths CODEOWNERS names -
workflows, actions, verification, compliance, infra/entra, infra/policy,
infra/purview, scripts/bootstrap - because those define what 'safe' MEANS and a
change to them can weaken the gate that authorised it.
Self-healing does NOT change. A security patch that GitHub generated for a named
advisory and that cleared the full gauntlet still auto-merges unattended in
operational mode; that is the product claim, not a development shortcut. Heal PRs
never touch the paths above, so the showpiece survives the transition intact.

ruleset.note: V1.5 reads GET /repos/{repo}/rules/branches/main and compares the pull_request rule's required_approving_review_count to enforcement[mode]. An identity that cannot read the rules reports SKIP, never 'the control is absent' (the F63/F105 rule).
